source.title: Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative Value Arbitrage Rule

claims.statement: Rank formation-period pairs by summed squared distance of normalized prices.
Open on a spread exceeding two formation standard deviations and unwind at the next price crossing.
Separate a twelve-month formation period from a six-month trading period.
claims.implementation: DistancePair.FORMATION and DistancePair.TRADING, represented by 252 and 126 sessions

chosen_variant: One closest pair from three symbols, 252 formation sessions and 126 trading sessions
adaptations: The source experiment selects several pairs from CRSP dividend-reinvested total-return histories; this sample selects one pair from three synthetic close series without dividends.

The paper reports one-dollar long and one-dollar short legs. This engine fixes each leg at 100 units of quote currency using signal-close prices and fills at next opening; later returns and corporate actions do not reproduce the paper's return accounting.
Orders for both legs are submitted together but fill independently on each symbol's next event; this engine does not guarantee atomic pair execution.

A final exit is signaled one session before the end of the trading interval to permit next-open execution. Delisting, staggered monthly portfolios and the original market results are outside this implementation.
